t: Reusable Component Generator - public implementations survey
title: Reusable Component Generator - public implementations survey
definition: Converts recurring implementation patterns into reusable components.
description:
Reusable Component Generator is one of the fundamental capabilities an AI needs to build things on demand: Converts recurring implementation patterns into reusable components. In the real world this capability is delivered by a rich ecosystem of tools, libraries and platforms. This database is the public edition - a fact-checked survey of the real implementations, the real techniques they share, the standards they follow, and laddered drills that teach the capability hands-on.

No single tool owns Reusable Component Generator. Competing implementations emphasize different trade-offs: speed against flexibility, simplicity against power, integration against independence. The implementation spotlights in this database document the notable real ones - what each does, where it excels, and how it serves Reusable Component Generator. Together they map the territory as it actually exists.

Every record carries a runnable demonstration program, because tools are understood by use. Run the demos with node, compare the implementations, practice the drills, and the Reusable Component Generator capability becomes something you can reach for - with full knowledge of which real tool fits which job.

definition: Architecture decision records as memory.
description:

In a Reusable Component Generator build it shows up when throughput matters more than novelty. Its architecture reflects hard-won lessons: small sharp pieces, explicit contracts between them, and no magic hidden from the operator. Knowing the surrounding technology is part of knowing the capability - the best Reusable Component Generator practitioners can say exactly where their tool ends and its neighbors begin.

t: Foundation drill - name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Reusable Componen
title: Foundation drill - name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Reusable Componen
definition: Ladder drill (foundation): name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Reusable Component Generator from a one-paragraph brief.
description:
Drill (FOUNDATION): name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Reusable Component Generator from a one-paragraph brief

Read the brief twice. List every input the Reusable Component Generator needs, every output it must produce, and one contract each input-output pair must satisfy. Work it by hand first, then run the demo program and compare its trace against your own reasoning. When they agree, the concept is yours.

Success criterion: you can list them from memory without looking at the brief
